title: Contract Configurator: per-customer data-location & subprocessor consent matrix
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: Enterprise customers increasingly ask for fine-grained guarantees: which subprocessors process data, where customer data is stored/processed (EU vs non-EU), and retention windows tied to contract tiers. Our current contract onboarding is binary (EU residency opt-in) and forces heavyweight legal negotiation for edge cases. Goal: build a self-serve contract configurator and consent matrix that lets Sales/Legal and customers select a combination of residency and subprocessor constraints at signup or during contract negotiation, surface the operational impact, and run A/B pricing experiments to quantify willingness-to-pay for stronger commitments. Scope: UI flow in Console and Sales portal, contract clause generator (templated SOW/DPA fragments), pricing delta calculator, backend flags for routing (region pinning + SCC activation), subprocessor allowlist/denylist support, and a minimal telemetry/analytics dashboard for experiment metrics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console: new 'Contract Configurator' step visible in Enterprise onboarding; 2) Customers or Sales can select: data-region preference (EU-only, EU+US, Global), retention tier (30/90/365 days), and per-subprocessor opt-in/opt-out; 3) Configurator emits a signed contract fragment and a human-readable summary; 4) Platform routes new customers to appropriate storage/processing regions and annotates requests with residency tags; 5) Pricing experiment runs with randomized assignment to control/variant showing calculated monthly delta and telemetry; 6) Legal has approved clause templates and there is a clear fallback path for unsupported combinations.
experiment_plan: Variant A (control): current binary residency opt-in, default pricing. Variant B: surface 3-tier retention + per-subprocessor opt-in with a visible pricing differential calculated from cost model. Variant C: add 'EU-only processing' top-tier with higher price and SCC auto-activation flow. Randomize new enterprise signups and a subset of renewals. Track conversion, time-to-sign, deal size, and support ticket volume. Run for 6 weeks then analyze uplift and legal/ops friction.
success_metrics: Primary: incremental ARR per customer cohort (30/60/90 day windows). Secondary: reduction in Legal review cycles for standard combos, decrease in average negotiation time, and increase in self-serve enterprise signups. Operational: correct routing rate > 99.5%, incident rate related to residency < 0.1% of requests.
approach: Phase 1: design PRD and clause templates with Legal; implement backend flags (region_pin, retention_tier, subprocessor_policy) and contract fragment generator. Phase 2: Console UI + Sales portal integration + experiment toggle. Phase 3: telemetry dashboard and pricing analysis. Engineering will implement soft-enforcement via routing metadata and a non-blocking guardrail from the runtime to surface mismatches; strict enforcement gated on Dedicated/Private availability. We'll limit initial subprocessor allowlist to top 10 partners and add an audit log for changes.
risks_mitigation: Risk: overly permissive UI leads to unsupported combos — mitigate with guardrails and 'not recommended' warnings. Risk: legal complexity across jurisdictions — mitigate by shipping a conservative set of pre-approved combos and routing edge-cases to Legal queue. Risk: runtime inability to guarantee EU-only processing for some features (third-party telemetry) — mitigate by documenting feature exclusions and offering Private deployment when strict guarantees required.
notes: Implementation notes: backend must persist contract choices as immutable contract_metadata on account entity. Runtime will read 'region_pin' and prefer EU endpoints; if not available fall back to 'best-effort' with an audit event. Pricing model inputs live in Optimize; link to cost-per-GB and per-token cost uplift for EU-only routing. Sales templates to include explicit language about subprocessor list changes with 30-day notice. UX should show expected SLA/latency delta when a choice increases routing cost.
next_steps: 1) Align clause templates with Legal (due 2026-03-08) 2) Engineering scoping & spike for runtime routing (ENG-21345) 3) Design Console mocks and validate with Sales (Elena to deliver mocks by 2026-03-10) 4) Toggle-based experiment groundwork in analytics (instrumentation + cohort assignment) 5) Legal sign-off and security review before launch.
